doc.title: Tom Malone interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 3, 2023

title: Lead trumpet with Brenda Lee and hitchhiking home
summary: Rowe reads an anecdote about a six-night gig in Jackson paying $16; Malone recalls his father's advice to wear a suit.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: There’s an anecdote in your bio, or this was an interview you did with somebody, I’m going to read it for a moment: “My first big time gig was playing lead trumpet with Brenda Lee at a club in Jackson, Mississippi. The gig was six nights a week. I always passed out after playing a big, long high C in the middle of the show. I had to hitchhike back and forth to Jackson every night. I was going to class every day in the morning. So every night from two to six AM I was waiting on the side of the road for a ride. The gig paid 16 dollars per night and I spent this time evaluating the music business.”
Yes. My father told me if you’re going to hitchhike wear a suit. So I had to wear a suit to the gig anyway so — but nobody picked me up until the sun came out.
